granular_contract_views.assessment: Battle-loot distribution credits each recorded living participant an equal positive stake share when total value permits, without checking the temporary flag. Thus a recorded living temporary participant can receive such a share if the participant and loot conditions are admitted. Ordinary inventory withdrawal separately debits that actor stake; temporary dismissal uses a different currency-transfer helper. Enrollment and liquid pool currency remain unproven.

The locked native Viewport uses physical-position/physical-size UVec2, not CSS pixels, with native depth0..1. SubCameraView retains full_size UVec2, offset Vec2 and size UVec2; proportional crop sizes are intentional. Native perspective and orthographic sub-view math uses those offsets and sizes directly, divides by full dimensions and derives projection bounds. It does not introduce a checked finite crop owner in the inspected methods. Zero-size and very large/cancelling f32 cases need real supported caller bounds before failure classification.

CanvasRect.apply clamps origin to target size and extent to remaining target size, disables the camera for zero extent, and otherwise installs native Viewport and SubCameraView with full dimensions at least1. granular_contract_views.assessment: Mission systems use CharacterId for tactical identity, TacticalCombatSide for affiliation, MissionState for lifecycle and a FrozenTerminal containing the generated strategic resolution and receipt. Query counts and loading status enter a transient TerminalCombatSnapshot. These visible owners should be reconciled with their constructors and native boundaries before introducing overlapping bespoke types; historical and selected systems bytes match.

The tactical CharacterId is a public u64 newtype identifying a strategic character, while a separate private reducer CharacterId wraps the same scalar. ConnectedPlayer carries the database Character and a two-variant TacticalMissionSide; player projection wraps the row ID and maps mission side to immutable TacticalCombatSide. Existing owners have distinct boundary roles; exact scalar admission and other consumers remain to reconcile.

The character table stores a u64 primary key. The rename reducer checks that the row exists and is alive before wrapping the ID in its private name-domain owner; the tactical receipt unwraps its CharacterId into the generated strategic scalar. Neither examined wrapper establishes a general nonzero character-ID invariant, and the separate zero-valued server assignment sentinel must not be conflated with character identity.

Player, NPC and starting-character insertion paths pass a u64 ID into the common creation function; that function checks child reservation consistency and inserts the supplied ID as the character key. The isolated starting-character helper accepts an externally reserved ID. No explicit nonzero check appears in these examined ranges; downstream custody semantics and all creation callers must be reconciled before deciding the identity domain.

Repair custody uses inventory character_id zero as an escrow sentinel and validates it as such; world event validation rejects zero for character actors and subjects. The examined common character insertion does not explicitly reject zero. These different native contracts require an explicit character identity policy and a distinct custody representation; actual zero-ID production and all consumers remain open.

The ordinary default-character generator forces a nonzero high-bit prefix, while default_character_with_id replaces it with a caller-supplied u64. The development-gated standalone seed accepts a character_id and, if absent, passes it through that helper into insertion. The inspected path has no explicit zero rejection before insertion, but later initialization may fail; a successful zero-ID transaction is not established.

Physical custody already owns CustodyCharacterId as NonZeroU64 and OperationalCustody as an enum distinguishing character, party, container, place and fixture. The persisted adapter validates character IDs on decode and re-encodes the scalar. This owner is a concrete candidate for reuse only where its operational-custody contract fits; the separate case CustodyObject ledger entry concerns legal case facts and is not the same contract.

Case CustodyObject distinguishes prefixed string AssetId and SubjectId, while its holder can be a character scalar or other legal disposition. The ID constructor validates prefix and characters, but the types derive transparent Deserialize rather than invoking that constructor. This is a separate case-fact admission question from nonzero physical CustodyCharacterId; actual native decode consumers and any existing alias require reconciliation.

The private custody_object adapter explicitly constructs and validates AssetId or SubjectId from native kind and string, matching existing queue entry 229. Separately, case objective expressions and stored outcome facts are decoded directly from JSON into typed structures; requirements include those same IDs and evaluation consumes decoded facts. Derived ID deserialization does not invoke the constructor. Other validation and native write paths remain to be checked before asserting reachable corrupt data.

Selected manual and diagnostic objective writers construct ObjectiveExpression and ObjectiveId before serializing; a generated-case writer serializes generated objectives. Outcome-fact insertion constructs validated fact and case IDs but receives its fact kind from an earlier path. These writes narrow the direct JSON decode concern, while generated objective and fact-kind provenance, imported data and other writers remain open.

Selected asset return, exchange, retrieval, subject rescue, release and capture producers reconstruct validated asset or subject IDs before recording facts. Dialogue decodes stored objectives, matches an authorized binding and checks custody before passing IDs to these validating producers. Hostile and challenge facts use other identities. Generated objective provenance, other producers and imported data remain open.

Selected generated rescue and recovery paths construct subject, asset and objective IDs through their constructors before assembling expressions. GeneratedCase derives Deserialize and contains those expressions, so constructor use during assembly alone does not establish validation for every decoded manifest. Other producer and import paths remain open.

Generated outcome and dialogue provenance validates metadata and manifest, deterministically regenerates it from the committed context, and compares generated objectives against case authority. Selected tests assert rejection of malformed and changed manifests. This constrains decoded IDs on these paths, but manual cases, other consumers and runtime test results remain open.

Investigation authority wrappers validate generated candidates and return (manifest JSON, context JSON), but generated_investigability destructures the second element as manifest and attempts to decode it as GeneratedCase. Its caller applies the hostile investigability modifier only on successful decoding. This is a concrete boundary mismatch and repair candidate; runtime impact and remaining consumers require verification.

Normally serialized GenerationContext and DeveloperGenerationContext omit required GeneratedCase fields, so decoding either context as the manifest fails and generated_investigability returns None. Source therefore skips the intended hostile investigability adjustment to terrain, awareness and stealth contributions; the adjustment is bounded and neutral at 50. Runtime verification remains outstanding.

facts: CanvasRect was moved from strategic_scene.protocol into a shared presentation module; both current strategic and map protocols import that same owner. The before strategic protocol133 and current65 are fully observed, as are both map protocol126 versions. Moving the declaration does not change the numeric admission or prove all native viewport consumers safe.

The locked native Viewport uses physical-position/physical-size UVec2, not CSS pixels, with native depth0..1. SubCameraView retains full_size UVec2, offset Vec2 and size UVec2; proportional crop sizes are intentional. Native perspective and orthographic sub-view math uses those offsets and sizes directly, divides by full dimensions and derives projection bounds. It does not introduce a checked finite crop owner in the inspected methods. Zero-size and very large/cancelling f32 cases need real supported caller bounds before failure classification.

CanvasRect.apply clamps origin to target size and extent to remaining target size, disables the camera for zero extent, and otherwise installs native Viewport and SubCameraView with full dimensions at least1. The native Viewport.clamp_to_size instead moves an outside origin just inside to one pixel. Those policies differ: do not replace the project operation with the native clamp blindly. Native projection fields are final lowering outputs; keep existing native types there.

Strategic sync_views obtains the current physical Window size and applies the region to retained or newly created live cameras. It returns early when requested view and retained scene are unchanged; window resize invalidation and cached offscreen camera allocation remain independent. Street/portrait paths use CacheWorld, whose internals were not read here. Reading the caller does not qualify snapshot GPU publication or resource-size limits.

Current strategic views test creates the street front as Position::from_metres(Vec3::ZERO).unwrap(), correcting the frozen raw-Vec3-versus-Position test expression noted in journal1418. Existing optional environment/atmosphere Some-to-None removal behavior is still a separate lifecycle question; this correction proves no runtime environment synchronization or build success.

facts: The observed production setup function creates one camera bundle per call with TacticalGameplayCamera, Camera3d, projection/transform and presentation settings. Its marker documentation describes the one interactive tactical camera. This is a concrete ordinary producer, not proof that a second arbitrary marker insertion or every reflected/debug/multi-window path is impossible. The binding itself has no single-camera enforcement.

Locked Bevy UI DefaultUiCamera first uses a single Camera with IsDefaultUiCamera. If there are multiple such cameras, it warns and falls back to the highest-order primary-window render target, breaking order ties by Entity. That fallback does not filter Camera.is_active. The project comments about inactive high-order selection therefore match the actual selector. Root UI nodes can separately use UiTargetCamera; the observed tactical root creation does not insert it and thus relies on default selection.

Locked EguiContexts.ctx_mut returns typed QuerySingleError when no primary context exists or multiple primaries exist; it does not silently choose an arbitrary primary. The project binding marks every matching added gameplay camera, so a multiple-camera population could violate native uniqueness. Ordinary producer evidence does not establish a live duplicate event, and no multi-camera failure was executed.

Without<EguiContext> means an added gameplay marker on a camera that already has an EguiContext receives neither native marker from this function. Added filtering means it is an initialization operation rather than a continuous reconciler; later marker/context removal, changing a camera role without a new addition, or competing markers need a separate ownership/lifecycle policy. Do not claim it continuously pins all possible states or that those alternative states are ordinary supported gameplay.

Native Egui initializes context mappings and screen rectangles in its ordered InitContexts set, before ProcessInput and BeginPass. This binding is only registered generally in PreUpdate, so the project does not declare an explicit relationship to InitContexts. Required-component hooks still construct native state once its queued insertion applies. First eligible input/UI-pass timing and deferred-command visibility should be checked after implementation if initialization ordering becomes part of the repair; no first-frame failure is claimed from source alone.

The persistent browser sync changes gameplay camera activity/viewport in PostUpdate when switching modes; it retains the same gameplay marker and context ownership. Tactical UI visibility and loading dismissal are separate mode consumers already source-qualified527. Do not change this binding into first-active-camera selection or assign tactical UI to strategic/offscreen cameras merely because they are currently active. Native Egui pipeline format/render support was not inspected here; the project comment about an incompatible float target is not treated as an executed or source-proven native format failure.

Retain the existing purpose-specific TacticalGameplayCamera owner and native PrimaryEguiContext/IsDefaultUiCamera markers. Document the ordinary singleton and initialization contract, and keep actual replacement/removal/multi-window/first-pass acceptance as explicit obligations.
